root_cause.text: The `mlo_scan_start_wk` delayed work queue was not being canceled when a virtual interface disconnected or changed state, allowing the work to execute after the vif structure was freed or in an inconsistent state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(mld->wiphy, &mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk)` in the `iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down()` function during station state transitions, and removes an ineffective cancellation from `iwl_mld_cleanup_vif()`. The CVE description explicitly states the work was "not canceled on disconnection" and could cause "use-after-free: if the work is executed after the vif is freed" or "init-after-queue issue" when `drv_change_interface` executes while the work is queued. The fix ensures the pending work is properly canceled before the vif state changes or is cleaned up.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant or problematic delayed work cancellation that was causing issues during VIF cleanup.
intent_record.what: Removed two lines: a call to wiphy_delayed_work_cancel() that cancels a delayed work item (mlo_scan_start_wk) and a blank line following it.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the cancellation of a pending delayed work task during VIF cleanup. The mlo_scan_start_wk work item will no longer be explicitly cancelled when a virtual interface is cleaned up, potentially allowing it to execute if it was scheduled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel mlo_scan_start_wk delayed work during station state transition to prevent stale work execution.
intent_record.what: Added two lines that call wiphy_delayed_work_cancel() to cancel the mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk delayed work item, following the existing pattern of canceling other delayed work items in the same code block.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the mlo_scan_start_wk delayed work is properly canceled when transitioning a station down in the iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down() function. Without this cancellation, the delayed work could potentially execute after the station state transition is complete, causing undefined behavior or resource leaks.
